title: Nomads of the steppe

match.reason: The closest bank point, his-genghis-khan-unites-mongols, mentions Mongol herders only in passing and is mainly about Temujin uniting the tribes and promotion by merit, so it is broader than the new point's focus on the nomadic lifestyle of tents and moving herds.

draft.title: Nomads of the steppe
card: The steppe is a huge area of dry grassland across Central Asia. It has few trees and cold winters, and it is better for grazing animals than for growing crops.
The Mongols were nomads. Nomads have no single permanent home. They move from place to place to find food and water.
The Mongols were herders. They kept horses, sheep, goats, cattle and camels, and used them for food, clothing and travel. They moved their herds to new pastures when the grass ran low.
Mongol families lived in round felt tents called gers (also known as yurts). A ger could be taken down, packed and carried to the next camp.
draft.remember: The Mongols were herders who lived in tents and moved with their animals across the grassland of the steppe.

a.q: Why did the Mongols move their camps several times a year?
opts: To find fresh grass for their animals
To stay close to fields of wheat and rice
To build stone towns in better places
To avoid the shade of thick forests
a.why: The Mongols were herders, and their animals needed fresh grass. When the grass ran low, they moved to new pastures. They did not farm crops, so fields of wheat and rice did not decide where they camped.
a.clue: Think about what the herds needed to eat.

b.q: Temur is a Mongol boy living on the steppe in the 1100s. Which home is he most likely to live in?
opts: A felt ger that his family can pack up and carry
A stone house in a village beside a river
A wooden hut in a forest clearing
A brick house inside a walled town
b.why: Nomads move often, so the Mongols needed homes they could take down and carry. A ger was made of felt and could be packed up easily. Stone and brick houses stay in one place, so they suit people who do not move.
b.clue: A nomad's home has to move with the family.

wants.brief: A photo of a traditional Mongolian ger (yurt) on open grassland, with a few grazing horses or sheep nearby, showing the round felt tent and the steppe landscape.
wants.why: Seeing the ger and the open grassland helps students picture how the Mongols lived.

a.best: To find fresh grass for their animals

b.best: A felt ger that his family can pack up and carry
